cls: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (fenamate / anthranilic acid derivative)
quick: 500 mg then 250 mg every 6 h, max 7 days
Take with food to reduce GI upset
GI symptoms, renal function, BP, CV risk
summary: Mefenamic acid is a fenamate NSAID for short-term relief of mild-to-moderate pain (<=7 days) and primary dysmenorrhea. Dosed 500 mg initially then 250 mg every 6 hours. Carries a boxed warning for serious cardiovascular and gastrointestinal events; use the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration.
indications: Relief of mild to moderate pain in patients >=14 years when therapy will not exceed one week (7 days)

dosage.d: 500 mg as initial dose, then 250 mg every 6 hours as needed
dosage.n: Usually not to exceed one week

dosage.d: 500 mg as initial dose, then 250 mg every 6 hours
dosage.n: Start at onset of menses/symptoms; up to 2-3 days

dosage.d: Use lowest effective dose; shortest duration

admin: Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration consistent with treatment goals
Take with food or milk to reduce gastrointestinal irritation
Do not exceed one week of therapy for pain
Avoid in the perioperative period of CABG surgery
Discontinue at the first appearance of skin rash or other hypersensitivity signs
moa: Inhibits cyclooxygenase enzymes (COX-1 and COX-2), reducing synthesis of prostaglandins that mediate pain, inflammation and uterine contractions. Mefenamic acid additionally antagonizes prostaglandin action at receptor sites, contributing to its efficacy in dysmenorrhea.

absolute: History of asthma, urticaria or allergic reaction to aspirin/other NSAIDs
Setting of coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery
Active GI bleeding or peptic ulceration
relative: Heart failure, hypertension or established cardiovascular disease

preg: Avoid use, especially at >=30 weeks gestation, due to risk of premature closure of the fetal ductus arteriosus and fetal renal dysfunction leading to oligohydramnios. Limit dose and duration if used between 20-30 weeks; generally avoid in late pregnancy.
lact: Avoid during breastfeeding; mefenamic acid passes into breast milk. If needed, use the lowest dose for the shortest time.
renal: Contraindicated in pre-existing renal disease. NSAIDs reduce renal prostaglandins and can cause acute kidney injury, especially with volume depletion, heart failure, or concomitant diuretics/ACE inhibitors.
hepatic: Use with caution; NSAIDs can cause elevations in transaminases and rarely severe hepatic reactions. Discontinue if liver disease develops or transaminases rise significantly.

major: Other NSAIDs / aspirin - additive GI toxicity
moderate: ACE inhibitors / ARBs / diuretics - reduced antihypertensive effect and renal injury ('triple whammy')
interactions.food: Take with food to reduce GI upset; food may slightly delay absorption.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid; increases risk of GI bleeding.
interactions.diagnostics: May cause a false-positive reaction for urinary bile (its metabolites); can raise transaminases.

rare: Severe skin reactions (Stevens-Johnson syndrome, TEN, DRESS)

monitoring: Signs and symptoms of GI bleeding (melena, hematemesis, anemia)
Renal function and blood pressure, especially in at-risk patients
Liver function if symptoms suggest hepatotoxicity
Cardiovascular status in patients with CV risk factors
counsel: Take with food; do not use for more than 7 days for pain
Stop and seek care for black/bloody stools, vomiting blood or severe stomach pain
Report chest pain, weakness or slurred speech (CV events)
Tell your doctor if pregnant; avoid in late pregnancy
pearls: Boxed warning: serious cardiovascular thrombotic and GI bleeding events.
Strictly short-term use - not more than 7 days for pain
Particularly effective for primary dysmenorrhea due to dual prostaglandin synthesis/action inhibition
Contraindicated with pre-existing renal disease and in CABG perioperative period
missed: If taken on a scheduled basis, take the missed dose when remembered unless the next dose is near; do not double up. As a short-term as-needed analgesic, simply resume when pain requires.
overdose: May cause lethargy, drowsiness, nausea, vomiting, epigastric pain, GI bleeding, seizures and renal failure; mefenamic acid overdose is notable for convulsions. Treat supportively with airway protection, activated charcoal if early, seizure control and renal monitoring; no specific antidote.
